key_insight: Optimization theory better explains practical machine learning when it preserves the actual objectives, gradient transformations, layer-wise geometry, and computational approximations used in training.
engineering_relevance: Reliable training requires aligning sketching with the objective, scheduling clipping appropriately, and tuning approximate orthogonalization precision jointly with the learning rate.
method: Analyze submodel training to distinguish biased updates from unbiased gradients of sketch-aware objectives.
Study quantile clipping and combine smoothed normalization with error compensation for private optimization.
Develop layer-wise generalized smoothness and the Gluon framework for Muon- and Scion-style methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence guarantees, fixed-point bias analysis, and validation of a layer-wise smoothness model, but names no datasets or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Coarser Muon orthogonalization requires smaller stepsizes, so reducing computation without retuning the learning rate may compromise optimization.
paper_title: Understanding Practical Optimization in Machine Learning
